step.prompt: In a city where consumer prices rise at 8% per year, using the Rule of 72, in approximately how many years will basic living costs double?
step.reveal: 9 years. 72 divided by an 8% inflation rate equals 9 years.
step.explanation: Using the Rule of 72: 72 / 8% = 9 years for prices to double.

step.prompt: With 0% interest and 10% annual inflation, by what percentage does the purchasing power of cash change after 3 years?
step.explanation: After 3 years at 10% inflation, real purchasing power drops to (1 / 1.10)^3 ≈ 75.1%, a loss of ~25%.

step.prompt: During a year of severe hyperinflation where consumer prices surge by 100%, what happens to the purchasing power of uninvested cash?
options: It is cut in half, buying 50% of what it bought a year ago
It becomes completely worthless, dropping to 0% purchasing power
It loses 100% of its nominal balance in the bank account
It loses only 10% of its purchasing power due to price controls
step.explanation: When price levels double (100% inflation), each unit of currency buys exactly half as much (1 / 2 = 50%).
